title: Inverse optimal control infers shared and patient-specific squat objectives after knee replacement
summary: Bi-level inverse optimal control inferred individual and shared movement-objective weights from recorded squats in six people after total knee replacement. Center-of-mass height and balance were dominant fitted terms, while balance weights varied across subjects; these are model-dependent inferences rather than direct measurements of neural control. The June 15, 2026 preprint reported within-sample trajectory reconstructions. A November 22 revision added leave-one-subject-out testing within the same six-person dataset, reporting mean RMSE 7.36° and correlation 0.95. Neither version establishes prediction from preoperative data, external-cohort generalization or improved clinical outcomes.
ai_technology: Bi-level inverse optimal control learning latent movement-objective weights from observed trajectories; OpenSim Moco forward model with PRIMA outer optimization

evidence.tested: Version 1 fitted individual and pooled objective weights to existing CAMS-Knee squat recordings from six participants, collected 64–87 months after surgery, and compared reconstructed hip, knee and ankle trajectories with those recordings. Its fitted center-of-mass-height and balance terms were dominant in most cases; balance weights ranged from 0.0950 to 0.4158. The version-2 abstract and author update note report leave-one-subject-out fitting on five subjects and testing on the sixth, repeated across the same cohort, with mean RMSE 7.36°, normalized RMSE 17.75% and Pearson correlation 0.95.
evidence.unknown: The inferred objective weights depend on the chosen cost terms, mechanical model, local optimization and simplified actuation; they do not directly measure human motor-control objectives. No independent external cohort, prospective prediction from preoperative inputs, improved patient outcome or independent replication is established. Uniform ligament parameters and imperfect movement-timing reproduction remain limitations.
evidence.ai_role: Inverse optimal control learns the weights of hypothesized movement objectives from observed human trajectories, enabling patient-specific and shared objective inference and reconstruction of squat kinematics. The fixed mechanical simulator and PRIMA optimization routine alone are not the enabling learned result.

source_review.scope: Independently read the complete primary version-1 article sections on inverse weight estimation, cohort, recovered weights, trajectory validation and limitations, plus version-2 primary abstract and author Summary of Updates. Version-2 full article body was not inspected. Version-specific text distinguishes the original within-sample result from later same-cohort cross-validation; the API repeats updated abstract content under earlier metadata.
